subject: botany

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack botany section, Chapter 9 'The Unit of Life' (book pp.23-26), which prints the question and a model answer but NO star rank and NO year citations - so stars are 0 and appearances are empty by fact, not by omission. steps.label: Who proposed it
lines: In 1838 Matthias Schleiden, a botanist,
examined many plants and concluded that all
plants are made of cells.
In 1839 Theodor Schwann, a zoologist, studied
animal tissues and found that animal cells
have a thin outer layer, the plasma membrane.
steps.why: Two workers on two different kingdoms reached the same conclusion, and that agreement between plants and animals is what made a general theory possible.
common_mistakes: Giving credit to Robert Hooke. Hooke first saw and named cells; he did not propose the theory.
Writing that Schleiden worked on animals. He was a botanist.
steps.memory_tip: Schleiden the botanist for plants in 1838, Schwann the zoologist for animals in 1839.
steps.margin_note: Both names with their subjects earns this mark.

steps.label: The theory
lines: Schleiden and Schwann together put forward the
cell theory.
They proposed that all living organisms are
composed of cells and of the products of
cells.
steps.why: The phrase 'and products of cells' is part of the original wording — it covers non-living material such as the cell wall and the matrix of a tissue.
common_mistakes: Leaving out 'products of cells'. It is part of the marked sentence.
Writing the modern three-point form here instead of the original statement.
steps.memory_tip: Cells, and the things cells make — that is the whole first statement.
steps.margin_note: Write the statement as a sentence, not as a list.

steps.label: Virchow's addition
lines: The theory could not explain how new cells
arise.
In 1855 Rudolf Virchow supplied the answer:
cells divide, and new cells are formed only
from pre-existing cells
(Omnis cellula-e cellula).
steps.why: The original theory said what organisms are made of but not where cells come from. Virchow closed that gap, and closing it is what completed the theory.
common_mistakes: Writing that Virchow proposed the cell theory. He extended it.
Giving the year as 1838. Virchow's addition is 1855.
steps.memory_tip: Schleiden and Schwann said what cells build; Virchow said where cells come from.
steps.margin_note: The Latin phrase is a bonus, not a requirement.

steps.label: Modern statement
lines: In its present form the cell theory states:
1) all organisms are made of one or more
cells,
2) the cell is the structural, functional and
hereditary unit of all living organisms,
3) all cells arise from pre-existing cells.
steps.why: The modern theory is the two original statements plus Virchow's, written as three numbered points — the form an examiner can tick quickly.
common_mistakes: Writing only that cells are the unit of life. The three points are separately marked.
Leaving out point 3, which is Virchow's contribution.
steps.memory_tip: Three points: made of cells, the cell is the unit, cells come from cells.
steps.margin_note: Number the three points; the examiner ticks them one by one.

insider_note: Dates and names carry marks in this question — 1838 Schleiden, 1839 Schwann, 1855 Virchow.
